package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-4367) in its font rendering code, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript code when a malicious PDF is opened. This enables remote code execution in any application or browser context using the vulnerable PDF.js library.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when rendering a PDF with a malicious fontMatrix)
execution_context.file_location: core font rendering logic (e.g., src/display/font_renderer.js or similar in pdfjs-dist)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code dynamically constructs a JavaScript function from PDF font rendering commands (cmds) using the Function constructor, with the function body derived from potentially attacker-controlled PDF metadata, leading to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of the Function constructor with untrusted input (cmds derived from PDF metadata) allows attackers to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript code if they control the PDF content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDF rendering should never execute arbitrary JavaScript from document metadata; it should only interpret font and drawing commands safely.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic function generation is sometimes used for performance optimization in trusted, internal code where all inputs are sanitized.
key_indicators: Use of new Function with attacker-controlled input
No sanitization or validation of cmds before code generation
Direct mapping of PDF metadata to executable JavaScript

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious PDF with a fontMatrix or cmds array containing JavaScript code as a string.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious data is loaded by the PDF.js renderer.

attack_chain.action: PDF.js processes the PDF and passes the attacker-controlled cmds to the font rendering logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: cmds array is used to generate JavaScript code.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code dynamically constructs a function using the Function constructor with the attacker-controlled cmds.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary JavaScript code is executed in the context of the application or browser.

attack_chain.action: Attacker's code runs with the privileges of the application, potentially leading to data theft, further exploitation, or system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: remote code execution and compromise of the host environment.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic function generation (new Function) with input derived from PDF file content
Execution of JavaScript code embedded in PDF font metadata
Unexpected alert() or network requests triggered during PDF rendering
file_indicators: PDF files with non-numeric or string values in fontMatrix or cmds arrays
Presence of pdf.js or pdfjs-dist versions below 4.2.67 in node_modules or application bundles
network_indicators: Outbound network requests initiated during PDF rendering (if attacker code exfiltrates data)
Unusual connections to domains not associated with normal PDF.js operation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for use of the Function constructor or eval in PDF.js code paths, especially where input is derived from PDF file content. Scan PDF files for suspicious fontMatrix or cmds values containing JavaScript code. Audit application dependencies for vulnerable pdfjs-dist versions. Implement runtime protections (e.g., CSP) to block dynamic code execution in PDF rendering contexts.
